title: Glutathione Assay Protocol
author: Peter Havel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ykcfusw
materials: Cover the plate with the plate cover provided.

Prepare the Assay Cocktail by mixing the following reagents in a 20 ml vial: MES Buffer (11.25 ml), reconstituted Cofactor Mixture (0.45 ml), reconstituted Enzyme Mixture (2.1 ml), water (2.3 ml), and reconstituted DTNB (0.45 ml). NOTE: The volumes of reagents given are for the use of the entire plate. Adjust the volumes of the reagents accordingly if only a part of the plate is used. Prepare fresh Assay Cocktail and run a standard curve each time the assay is performed. Use the Assay Cocktail within 10 minutes of preparation.

steps.title: Add Standards to Plate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of Standard (tubes A-H) per well in the designated wells on the plate according to the Sample Plate Format.

steps.title: Add Samples to Plate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of sample to each of the sample wells.

steps.title: Add Assay Cocktail and Incubate
steps.instruction: Add 150 µl of freshly prepared Assay Cocktail to each well containing standards and samples using a multichannel pipette, then incubate in the dark on an orbital shaker.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 150 µl of Assay Cocktail per well

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance in the wells at 405-414 nm using a plate reader.

substeps.instruction: For kinetic measurement: Measure at five minute intervals for 30 minutes (6 measurements total)
For end point method: One measurement at 25 minutes is sufficient

steps.title: Calculate GSH Concentration (End Point Method)
steps.instruction: Determine the GSH concentration of samples using the End Point Method.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the average absorbance from the 25 minutes measurement for each standard and sample
Subtract the absorbance value of standard A from itself and all other values to obtain the corrected absorbance
Plot the corrected absorbance values of each standard as a function of the concentration of GSSG or Total GSH
Calculate the values of GSSG or Total GSH for each sample from the standard curve
If the sample required deproteination, multiply the result by 2 to account for the addition of MPA Reagent
